notes:
The delegate spoke to various videos put together which speak to the frequency of truck traffic on his street. items.title: Joe Salemi, Executive Director, Landscape Ontario Horticultural Trades Association
notes:
The delegate spoke in favour of a motion listed on the agenda which seeks to reduce salt pollution in the Region. He alluded to some of the issues associated with the market and contracting for road salting services, such as concerns related to insurance and liability. The delegate indicated that the road salt and snow removal industry is asking for regulations which identify hazards and which balances responsibilities for property owners and snow removal contractors.

In response to a question from the Committee, J. Salemi indicated his organization has been in discussion with the province to change the legislation to equalize liability for contractors and property owners. Through a private members bill, the statute of limitations has been altered to 60 days for slips and falls, though loopholes still exist.

Replying to a question from the Committee, J. Salemi answered that his organization does not look at windshield fluid and other pollution impacts, but that could be an area for exploration.

Responding to a question from the Committee, J. Salemi spoke to how salt management may affect accessibility, explaining that packing snow on walkways and passageways is not a best practice and that training is in place for the industry to avoid this occurrence, with data showing that correct amounts of salt are known to get clear pavement.

attachments.name: BRIEFING NOTE - Landscape Ontario’s Snow and Ice Management Sector - Salt Pollution Motion.pdf

items.title: Claire Malcolmson, Executive Director, Rescue Lake Simcoe Coalition
notes:
The delegate appeared to provide information on the initiatives her organization is involved in, urging action be taken to protect water in the province from salt pollution. The delegate and her organization support the motion listed on the agenda regarding salt pollution management. She mentioned that with growing road networks, more salt could affect more waterways, which needs to be addressed. The delegate elaborated on the ecological impact of salt usage based on impact on aquatic species.

In reply to a question from the Committee, the delegate indicated there are groups out there who should be consulted on limited liability legislation, and that her organization is heavily focused on the environmental impact and cost effectiveness. She answered that she would prefer limited liability piece remain in the motion, since the provincial government has not acted fully in protection of the environment.

Responding to a question from the Committee, the delegate provided that the Source Water Protection Act protects against contaminants which differs by area, which results in different contaminant prevention plans.

items.title: PDL-GDS-25-005, Year-End 2024 Population and Household Estimates for Waterloo Region
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, spoke to the annual cycle of reports associated with this report that speaks to growth. He provided that the Region's population grew at a slower rate than 2023, due especially to the reduction in the international student population resulting from changes in federal policy. R. Regier indicated there has been an increase in building permit activity.

Responding to questions, Ryan Pogrzeba, Manager, Growth Management and Analytic Services spoke to what constitutes non-residential builds and explained that a discrepancy in census data to the data presented in the report comes from estimates based on averages. R. Regier elaborated that because population is changing over time, road signs that speak to populations in given municipalities provide a forecast for the end of the year population growth.

Replying to a question from the Committee, Tim Brubacher, Deputy Clerk/Manager, Council and Administrative Services, answered as to how population data was used for Regional Council composition reviews, indicating a review will need to be done after the 2026 election.

In response to a question from the Committee, R. Pogrzeba indicated projection numbers typically align with census years.

In reply to a question from the Committee, R. Pogrzeba provided that adjustments to immigration rates and international student intake rates are based on available information, and thus reflective of current federal policy.

Received for information.

items.title: PDL-GDS-25-004, 2025-2030 Corporate Climate Change Action Plan
notes:
R. Regier provided an introduction to the report, explaining that the Region has been working with the community to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and elaborated on the work done to accomplish this. Danielle De Fields, Director, Regional Growth, Development and Sustainability Services, introduced the presentation, providing an overview of the strategy. Meaghan Eastwood, Manager, Manager, Planning and Sustainability, spoke to the effects of climate change, including the impact on population trends and displacement, as well as on species extinction. She underscored the impact climate change is already having on the environmental, public health, and financial aspects. M. Eastwood provided that the plan is designed specifically designed to reduce GHG emissions in alignment with the Region's strategic plan, highlighting the 25-year anticipated decarbonization if the various phases are implemented. Katelyn Tozer, Supervisor, Climate Transition & Sustainability, spoke to action being conducted based on various theme areas within the Region, as well as costs that impact long-term financial planning. She indicated this plan will continue to be reviewed.

In reply to a question from the Committee, M. Eastwood answered that Climate Action WR is relied upon to engage the community on these measures, with affordable transit services being identified as a major factor.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner explained that hybrid buses were authorized to be purchased in 2024 and more work is underway to convert available buses to be more environmentally efficient. M. Eastwood provided that a standardized consistent approach will be sought regarding report formatting for staff.

In response to a question from the Committee, M. Eastwood indicated that carbon emissions that come from the airport are not specifically regionally controlled nor included in their modelling. She further explained that programs are in place to measure and attempt to mitigate scope 3 emissions through the Airport Decarbonization Action Plan.

items.title: EES-FFM-25-001, Electrification of WRH Water Heaters
notes:
J. Rose introduced the report, explaining how the Region is working towards its climate goals, elaborating on how the electrification of water heaters at Waterloo Region Housing will impact the budget and tenants. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, J. Rose answered the Region owns the water heaters. She further indicated that the impact to the average household estimate is over a 10 year period, and based on assumptions on electricity and gas rates. Furthermore, she provided that staff are recommending a pilot project to allow the Region to determine whether financial assumptions are correct. Staff will report back on the results and gas lines will not be removed during the project.

In reply to a question from the Committee, J. Rose explained that the team in charge of the pilot will look at costs as a whole. Peter Sweeney, Commissioner, Community Services, added that Waterloo Regional Housing facilities need a consistent approach to heating, with the idea being to move through the first phase and ensure residents are made whole. The first phase is two years.

Responding to a question from the Committee, J. Rose answered that rebates would be available for tenants with higher electricity bills as a result of the electrification of water heaters. The housing team will look at utilities in general. J. Rose provided that the replacement is based on the life of the water heater itself.

Replying to a question from the Committee, Wayne Steffler, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, indicated that the capital $17,400 difference is an estimate based on utility rates. Additionally, the rates can change significantly on a continual basis. J. Rose clarified that each year will be different due to different quantities being replaced.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
TSD-TRP-25-006, Cambridge Truck Diversion Project Evaluation - 2025 Update
notes:
D. Spooner provided an overview of the results of the truck diversion project in Cambridge, notiung that it has largely been a success, but has had some consequences for residents on a portion of Ainslie Street. He spoke to the presence of trucks in the area, and highlighted the potential solutions based on their viability. D. Spooner indicated that solutions will continue to be explored.

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner explained that land-use patterns are looked at to develop mobility plans and infrastructure improvements. An update was requested for the plausibility of a fourth bridge as well as enforcement in the relevant area.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner clarified the reasoning for the deferral of a project from 2018, adding that the integrated mobility plan will revisit land use forecasts and look at areas of greatest needs based on models and the results of those models.

In response to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner spoke to enforcement working with other organizations such as Waterloo Regional Police Services (WRPS). D. Spooner clarified that blitzes do occur by WRPS in the area, and that additional monitoring can occur through Miovision. He noted that the Region can ask for additional enforcement.

Replying to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner indicated that his staff prefer that more changes happen as part of the integrated mobility plan. D. Spooner explained that the challenges come not with diversion itself but where trucks go afterward.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - Councillor D. McCabe
motions.text: WHEREAS road salt is a known toxic substance designated under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act because of tangible threats of serious or irreversible environmental and health damage from road salt; and WHEREAS salt levels in Ontario’s groundwater aquifers, creeks, rivers, and lakes have increasingly worsened since the 1970s, seriously affecting municipal drinking water sources and aquatic life; and WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo, in collaboration with local municipalities, is actively attempting to mitigate salt pollution using existing policies, programs and site design measures that would be significantly more effective with supporting Provincial legislation; and WHEREAS the Ontario and Canadian governments have taken many actions over the past 25 years including setting water quality guidelines, developing voluntary codes of practice, signing the Canada-Ontario Great Lakes Agreement, and holding workshops, yet still the salt problem continues to grow; and WHEREAS numerous situation analyses have recommended salt solutions involving liability protection, contractor certification, government approved Best Management Practices (BMPs) and salt management plans; and WHEREAS increased numbers of slips and falls claims, and other injury/collision claims related to snow and ice, are resulting in salt applicators overusing salt beyond levels considered best practices; and WHEREAS unlimited contractor liability is making it difficult or expensive for snow and ice management contractors to obtain insurance coverage, resulting in contractors leaving the business, thereby making it difficult for municipalities and private owners to find contractors; and WHEREAS the Snow and Ice Management Sector (SMS) of Landscape Ontario is working with the Ontario government to institute a limited liability regime for snow and ice management, including enforceable contractor training/certification and government-approved BMPs for salt application; and WHEREAS many Ontario municipalities have Salt Management Plans, but these often require updating considering improved science and better salt management practices now available. THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: The Region of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to work on a priority basis with key stakeholders to develop limited liability legislation, including enforceable contractor training and a single set of provincially-endorsed standard BMPs for snow and ice management; and The Region of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to create and fund an expert stakeholder advisory committee to advise the province and municipalities on the best courses of action to protect freshwater ecosystems and drinking water from the impacts of salt pollution; and This resolution be sent to all municipalities in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO), Ontario Big City Mayors Caucus (OBCM), Landscape Ontario, Conservation Ontario, the Minister of the Environment Conservation and Parks (MECP), the Minister of Red Tape Reduction, the Attorney General, and Premier Doug Ford.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS road salt is a known toxic substance designated under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act because of tangible threats of serious or irreversible environmental and health damage from road salt; and

WHEREAS salt levels in Ontario’s groundwater aquifers, creeks, rivers, and lakes have increasingly worsened since the 1970s, seriously affecting municipal drinking water sources and aquatic life; and

WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo, in collaboration with local municipalities, is actively attempting to mitigate salt pollution using existing policies, programs and site design measures that would be significantly more effective with supporting Provincial legislation; and

WHEREAS the Ontario and Canadian governments have taken many actions over the past 25 years including setting water quality guidelines, developing voluntary codes of practice, signing the Canada-Ontario Great Lakes Agreement, and holding workshops, yet still the salt problem continues to grow; and

WHEREAS numerous situation analyses have recommended salt solutions involving liability protection, contractor certification, government approved Best Management Practices (BMPs) and salt management plans; and

WHEREAS increased numbers of slips and falls claims, and other injury/collision claims related to snow and ice, are resulting in salt applicators overusing salt beyond levels considered best practices; and

WHEREAS unlimited contractor liability is making it difficult or expensive for snow and ice management contractors to obtain insurance coverage, resulting in contractors leaving the business, thereby making it difficult for municipalities and private owners to find contractors; and

WHEREAS the Snow and Ice Management Sector (SMS) of Landscape Ontario is working with the Ontario government to institute a limited liability regime for snow and ice management, including enforceable contractor training/certification and government-approved BMPs for salt application; and

WHEREAS many Ontario municipalities have Salt Management Plans, but these often require updating considering improved science and better salt management practices now available.

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

  1. The Region of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to work on a priority basis with key stakeholders to develop limited liability legislation, including enforceable contractor training and a single set of provincially-endorsed standard BMPs for snow and ice management; and
  2. The Region of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to create and fund an expert stakeholder advisory committee to advise the province and municipalities on the best courses of action to protect freshwater ecosystems and drinking water from the impacts of salt pollution; and
  3. This resolution be sent to all municipalities in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO), Ontario Big City Mayors Caucus (OBCM), Landscape Ontario, Conservation Ontario, the Minister of the Environment Conservation and Parks (MECP), the Minister of Red Tape Reduction, the Attorney General, and Premier Doug Ford.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - Councillor M. Rodrigues
motions.text: WHEREAS Waterloo Region experienced multiple significant weather events in Winter 2024/2025, resulting in the greatest annual snowfall accumulations since 2008; WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo coordinates winter maintenance of the public right-of-way across multiple operators; WHEREAS timely and appropriate winter maintenance of the public right-of-way is vital for supporting year-round accessibility for all residents and businesses -- particularly those who walk and roll, active transportation users, transit riders, and emergency vehicles; AND WHEREAS responsive and well-coordinated winter maintenance of the public right-of-way is a core municipal service susceptible to variable weather patterns and a changing climate; THEREFORE be it resolved that the Commissioner of Transportation conduct a review of Winter 2024/2025 maintenance operations and prepare a Report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee prior to the 2026 Plan and Budget process, which: Reviews existing winter maintenance operational standards and agreements to determine how to optimize existing available resources; Investigates and reports on specific issues and coordination opportunities for infrastructure under Regional jurisdiction including but not limited to coordination of snow clearing and overhead ice build-up along the ION LRT corridor and snow clearing of separated cycling tracks and lanes, sidewalks and multi-use trails along Regional Roads, and transit stops; Identifies potential improvements to the Region's winter maintenance programs, policies, and agreements for Council’s consideration; and Establishes a reporting process to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee prior to the Plan and Budget cycle, outlining performance of winter operations from the previous season and insights around operational efforts and future continuous improvements.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS Waterloo Region experienced multiple significant weather events in Winter 2024/2025, resulting in the greatest annual snowfall accumulations since 2008;

WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo coordinates winter maintenance of the public right-of-way across multiple operators;

WHEREAS timely and appropriate winter maintenance of the public right-of-way is vital for supporting year-round accessibility for all residents and businesses -- particularly those who walk and roll, active transportation users, transit riders, and emergency vehicles;

AND WHEREAS responsive and well-coordinated winter maintenance of the public right-of-way is a core municipal service susceptible to variable weather patterns and a changing climate; 

THEREFORE be it resolved that the Commissioner of Transportation conduct a review of Winter 2024/2025 maintenance operations and prepare a Report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee prior to the 2026 Plan and Budget process, which:

  1. Reviews existing winter maintenance operational standards and agreements to determine how to optimize existing available resources;
  2. Investigates and reports on specific issues and coordination opportunities for infrastructure under Regional jurisdiction including but not limited to coordination of snow clearing and overhead ice build-up along the ION LRT corridor and snow clearing of separated cycling tracks and lanes, sidewalks and multi-use trails along Regional Roads, and transit stops;
  3. Identifies potential improvements to the Region's winter maintenance programs, policies, and agreements for Council’s consideration; and
  4. Establishes a reporting process to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee prior to the Plan and Budget cycle, outlining performance of winter operations from the previous season and insights around operational efforts and future continuous improvements.
